correctness.rationale: For each index i, the two closed-neighborhood counts are exactly q+1_{i in P}-1_{i in Q} and p+1_{i in Q}-1_{i in P}. Since the difference term lies in {-1,0,1}, the only sub-k side-size possibility is the k=1 full-side exception; at the boundary p=k or q=k the inequalities reduce exactly to one index-set inclusion. The enumerator follows by a disjoint interior/boundary decomposition with one diagonal subtraction. Exhaustive checks for n=3..8 and all feasible k agree with the characterization, bivariate coefficients, univariate coefficients, and minimum counts.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a standard symmetric family, also appearing as bipartite Kneser graphs and bipartite double covers of complete graphs, while k-tuple domination models uniform multiple coverage and has fault-tolerance motivation. The theorem gives the complete feasible-family structure simultaneously for every multiplicity k, a side-sensitive bivariate enumerator, and exact minimum counts. This is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice or a recomputation of a known table.
